desc: Read the input $N$ and the list $S$, then sort $S$ in ascending order.
Create a boolean lookup array (or hash set) of size $10^6 + 1$ to mark the presence of each number in $S$ for $O(1)$ lookups.
Initialize a counter to zero and iterate through each number $B$ in $S$ treating it as the middle element of a potential triplet.

For each $B$, iterate through possible differences $d$ starting from 1 up to $B-1$ (or until $B+d$ exceeds the maximum possible value in $S$); if both $B-d$ and $B+d$ exist in the lookup structure, increment the counter.
Implement an iterative FFT in Python.
Read input, create a polynomial $P(x) = \sum_{i \in S} x^i$.
Iterate through $B \in S$, add $(Q[2B] - 1) / 2$ to the answer.
Run the code against the provided sample inputs to verify correctness.
Ensure the solution handles edge cases (e.g., $N < 3$, small values of $S_i$).
If performance is an issue with pure Python FFT, consider optimizations (though the current implementation is standard).
